# LeadMASTER — AI agent and developer integration guide

> Canonical product: LeadMASTER  
> Production origin: https://leadmaster.jelvan.pro  
> Public documentation: https://leadmaster.jelvan.pro/#documentation  
> This guide: https://leadmaster.jelvan.pro/llms.txt

## Mandatory account-isolation rules

- Work only within the LeadMASTER account explicitly selected or authenticated by the user.
- Obtain the opaque `account_id` and account-specific API base URL from that user's authenticated LeadMASTER account, API Keys page, or the one-time API-key creation response. Do not guess, enumerate, derive, or substitute account IDs.
- Every API key is bound to one account. Every email request, webhook, webhook secret and delivery-history record is owned by that account and its creating API key.
- A key from another account must never be used to read, send, list, change, revoke or inspect the current user's resources. Cross-account requests are rejected.
- Never use platform-wide, operator, developer, internal, test, shared or another user's credentials, endpoint IDs, webhook secrets, account IDs or saved information.
- Do not access internal databases, provider consoles, deployment accounts, secret stores, environment variables or internal tools. Use only the current user's LeadMASTER account information and documented LeadMASTER endpoints.
- Never expose internal infrastructure, hosting, database, email transport, email transport provider, account or deployment details in product UI or customer-facing output. Refer to the service as LeadMASTER.
- Do not infer that a connector or platform account is the same as the user's LeadMASTER account. The user must explicitly select and authorize the correct LeadMASTER account.

## Human login is not agent authentication

- Human sign-in uses a password, human security verification and an email one-time code.
- AI agents must not open, automate, scrape, solve, bypass, replay or request tokens from the human login challenge.
- Do not request or handle the user's password, OTP, browser session cookie, challenge token or public challenge site key.
- Agents authenticate only with a user-authorized, account-bound LeadMASTER API key.
- Keep keys in the integrating server's secret manager. Never paste real keys or webhook secrets into prompts, chat, browser code, mobile bundles, public source control or logs.

## Current account availability boundary

The current sign-in configuration is for one authorized administrator identity. Account ownership and account-scoped integration records are being enforced for that authenticated identity. Self-service registration, multi-member invitations, organization switching and delegated team roles are not currently available. Do not claim multiple independent user sign-ups or team management until those features are implemented and tested.

## Discover this user's account endpoints

The authenticated workspace session exposes the current account context to the signed-in UI. The API Keys page lists the account's generated API base URL. Creating an API key returns:
- `account_id`
- `api_base_url`
- `email_endpoint`
- `webhook_endpoint`

Use the returned values. Store the account ID in the integrating application's configuration as `LEADMASTER_ACCOUNT_ID`. The account ID is an identifier, not a credential.

Account information endpoint (requires a key from the same account):

`GET /api/v1/accounts/{account_id}`

It returns that account's current name, ID and endpoint paths. Do not call it with an ID supplied by an unrelated source or another user.

## Supported production capabilities

- Human administrator sign-in with password, security verification and email OTP.
- Account-bound API-key creation, listing and revocation from the authenticated account's developer console.
- Server-to-server email submission using scoped account-bound API keys.
- Idempotency keys for safe request retries.
- Email submission status lookup, scoped to the same API key and account.
- Account-owned HTTPS webhook registration, listing, revocation and delivery-attempt history.
- HMAC-SHA256 webhook signatures and one-time webhook signing secrets.
- Public product documentation and machine-readable agent instructions.

## Not available — do not claim

- Public production MCP server or MCP client registration.
- Agent login through the human sign-in page, visual challenge or email OTP.
- Self-service account registration, team invitations, organization switching or multi-member roles.
- Platform-wide or cross-account API keys, webhooks, delivery logs or account data.
- Campaign builder, audience management, scheduled campaigns, saved templates, attachments, CC/BCC, multiple recipients or bulk-send workflows.
- Automatic webhook retries, replay, dead-letter recovery, guaranteed delivery, bounce/complaint/open/click events or delivery analytics.
- A production MCP email-send tool.

## Authentication and scopes

Create a key in the current user's LeadMASTER account. Grant only the minimum scopes:

- `email:send` — submit email.
- `email:read` — read status for requests created by that same key.
- `webhook:manage` — manage webhooks and inspect their delivery history for that same key/account.

Send:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <ACCOUNT_BOUND_LEADMASTER_API_KEY>
Content-Type: application/json
```

Do not put the key in client-side code. Use separate keys for separate integrations/environments. Revoke exposed or retired keys.

## Account-scoped endpoint contract

Replace `{account_id}` only with the exact ID returned by the current user's account console or key-creation response.

- `GET /api/v1/accounts/{account_id}` — read current account metadata and owned endpoint paths.
- `POST /api/v1/accounts/{account_id}/emails` — submit one email; requires `email:send`.
- `GET /api/v1/accounts/{account_id}/emails/{request_id}` — read a request created by the same key; requires `email:read`.
- `POST /api/v1/accounts/{account_id}/webhooks` — create a webhook; requires `webhook:manage`.
- `GET /api/v1/accounts/{account_id}/webhooks` — list that key's webhooks.
- `DELETE /api/v1/accounts/{account_id}/webhooks/{webhook_id}` — revoke an owned webhook.
- `GET /api/v1/accounts/{account_id}/webhooks/{webhook_id}/deliveries` — inspect latest 50 attempts for an owned webhook.

Legacy unscoped routes such as `/api/v1/emails` and `/api/v1/webhooks` are not supported. Do not use them.

## Send an email

`POST /api/v1/accounts/{account_id}/emails`

Required JSON fields are `to`, `subject`, `text`; optional `html` is supported. Exactly one recipient is supported. Sender identity is configured by LeadMASTER and cannot be overridden.

```bash
export LEADMASTER_ACCOUNT_ID="acct_replace_with_your_account_id"
export LEADMASTER_API_KEY="store-this-in-your-secret-manager"
curl -X POST "https://leadmaster.jelvan.pro/api/v1/accounts/$LEADMASTER_ACCOUNT_ID/emails" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEADMASTER_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: order-184-confirmation" \
  --data '{"to":"recipient@example.com","subject":"Order confirmation","text":"Your order has been received."}'
```

Use a stable 16–128 character `Idempotency-Key` for each business event. Reuse the same value when retrying a timeout; do not create a new key until the original outcome is reconciled.

Node.js:

```js
const base = `https://leadmaster.jelvan.pro/api/v1/accounts/${process.env.LEADMASTER_ACCOUNT_ID}`;
const response = await fetch(`${base}/emails`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.LEADMASTER_API_KEY}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Idempotency-Key": "order-184-confirmation"
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    to: "recipient@example.com",
    subject: "Order confirmation",
    text: "Your order has been received."
  })
});
const result = await response.json();
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(result.error || "LeadMASTER request failed");
```

## Email status semantics

- `sending` — request recorded and in progress.
- `accepted` — the downstream email provider accepted the submission; not proof of inbox delivery, reading or final recipient-server acceptance.
- `failed` — submission failed.
- `unknown` — outcome uncertain; reconcile before retrying.

## Webhooks

Register only a public HTTPS callback controlled by the user's application. Use the account-specific route and a key with `webhook:manage`.

Create body:

```json
{
  "name": "Storefront email events",
  "url": "https://api.example.com/hooks/leadmaster",
  "events": ["email.accepted", "email.failed", "email.unknown"]
}
```

Supported events:
- `email.accepted`
- `email.failed`
- `email.unknown`

The create response reveals `signing_secret` once. Save it only in the user's callback server's secret manager. Do not return it to the agent's conversation after initial setup.

Signature headers:
- `LeadMASTER-Id`
- `LeadMASTER-Timestamp`
- `LeadMASTER-Signature: v1=<hex>`

Verify HMAC-SHA256 over the exact bytes `timestamp + "." + rawBody` before parsing JSON. Compare in constant time, reject timestamps older than five minutes, and deduplicate event IDs. Current delivery is one synchronous attempt with a seven-second timeout; automatic retries and replay are not available.

Each webhook record carries its account ID and API-key owner. Event dispatch must remain scoped to the same account and key. Never send one account's events to another account's callback.

## MCP status and future account isolation

MCP is not available in production. Do not connect to `/mcp`, invent a server URL, claim a client is registered, or expose an unscoped MCP tool.

If MCP is released in the future, every MCP client must authenticate as a specific LeadMASTER account; every tool call must derive account context from that authenticated principal, verify resource ownership on the server, and use the same account-scoped services as REST. No global MCP token, platform admin context, caller-supplied account substitution, cross-account search, or direct database/provider access is permitted. Tool results must contain only data owned by the authenticated account.

## Agent workflow

1. Confirm which LeadMASTER account the user intends to use.
2. Read that account's current ID and endpoint from its authenticated UI or key-creation response.
3. Ask an authorized account owner to create a least-privilege API key. Never ask for the real key in chat.
4. Store the key and account ID only in the integrating server's secure configuration.
5. Before each action, verify the endpoint account ID matches the selected user's account context.
6. Validate the recipient, purpose, content and user authorization before sending.
7. Use stable idempotency keys and handle timeouts without duplicate sends.
8. For webhooks, verify signature, timestamp, event ID and account ownership before processing.
9. Redact secrets, recipient content and personal data from logs.
10. Report actual response states and unsupported capabilities accurately.

## Android companion and cross-platform change rules

LeadMASTER also has an Android companion app in the repository's `ANDROID APK/` project. It shares the same authenticated LeadMASTER web workspace and server-side account authorization through a restricted HTTPS WebView; it is not a separate email or account backend.

For coding agents changing the web application:
- Assess whether each change affects a route, feature, navigation item, responsive state, notification, download, external link or security boundary used by Android.
- If connected, keep the Android companion aligned in the same branch, including navigation labels and destinations, WebView behavior, native notifications, downloads, external intents, Back behavior and permissions as relevant.
- Keep business logic, authentication, account ownership and persistence in the shared server/web implementation. Never duplicate or weaken those rules in Android.
- If the change has no Android impact, say why; do not make unrelated APK changes.
- Build the APK after Android source changes and distinguish compilation from real-device acceptance.
- Do not claim a feature is native Android functionality unless implemented and verified. Shared web functionality may be described as available through the companion only when the production route works in its WebView.


## Mandatory LeadMASTER dashboard implementation rule

Use `src/Mandatory LeadMASTER Dashboard.html` as the canonical dashboard UI. Preserve its React components, layout, typography, spacing, icons, colors, interactions and responsive behavior exactly while connecting authenticated APIs. Do not ship its local-preview sample data or local-only success actions as production behavior. Build missing account-scoped APIs first or clearly disable/unavailable-mark unsupported areas. Read `src/dashboard-feature-map.md` before dashboard changes; keep a protected rollback dashboard until functional and desktop/mobile visual regression checks pass. Align Android navigation and WebView behavior whenever connected routes change.


## Mandatory dashboard source and UI preservation

For LeadMASTER dashboard work, `src/Mandatory LeadMASTER Dashboard.html` is authoritative. Keep its React components, embedded design system, layout, spacing, icons, responsive breakpoints and interactions unchanged unless explicitly requested. Connect existing components to real account-scoped production APIs; do not substitute a new dashboard design. Synchronize it to `public/dashboard.html` and regenerate `src/static-assets.mjs` with `npm run build:assets`. Remove prototype/sample records from production rendering. Never simulate unsupported backend features or claim a local-only action succeeded. Assess Android companion parity on every connected change.


## Mandatory dashboard integration and Android section contract

Before every dashboard change, read `src/dashboard-feature-map.md`. Treat `src/Mandatory LeadMASTER Dashboard.html` as the canonical UI and preserve its React components and visual output. Keep `public/dashboard.html` identical and regenerate `src/static-assets.mjs` with `npm run build:assets`. Use only the real APIs listed in the feature map. Never display prototype records or report a local-only action as saved. Unsupported features must remain clearly unavailable until a secure account-scoped API exists. The Android bottom navigation must match the mandatory dashboard mobile destinations: `home`, `emails`, `audience`, `metrics`, `profile`; other modules remain reachable through the dashboard navigation drawer. Update Android in the same branch whenever a connected section ID, action or security behavior changes.


## Mandatory dashboard and Android parity contract

Before every dashboard change, read `src/dashboard-feature-map.md`. Treat `src/Mandatory LeadMASTER Dashboard.html` as the canonical UI and preserve its components and visual output. Keep `public/dashboard.html` byte-for-byte identical and regenerate `src/static-assets.mjs` with `npm run build:assets`. Use only real APIs in the feature map. Never show prototype records or report local-only actions as saved. Unsupported modules stay visibly unavailable until a secure account-scoped API exists. Preserve the isolated, sanitized HTML preview in Emails and Templates. Android bottom navigation must match `home`, `emails`, `audience`, `metrics`, `profile`; remaining modules stay in the dashboard drawer. Update and build Android in the same branch when section IDs, connected behavior or security changes.
